atlas-es.0204: Hiring from abroad needs a job on the hard-to-fill occupations list or a certificate that no resident candidate was found; a full-time contract of at least a year at no less than the minimum wage.
atlas-es.0205: First permit for one year; the first renewal is for four, and after five years comes long-term residence.
atlas-es.0207: €203.84, or €407.71 above twice the minimum wage
atlas-es.0208: The employer must register you with social security within three months of your arrival, or the permit lapses.
atlas-es.0210: A university or research centre signs a hosting agreement and applies online; the decision comes within 20 working days and silence means yes. The permit lasts up to three years and counts towards Spanish citizenship.
atlas-es.0211: Since August 2026 PhD students on a pre-doctoral contract or a qualifying scholarship come as researchers, not on a student visa.
atlas-es.0212: Spain has working-holiday agreements only with Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea.
atlas-es.0213: Only for citizens of Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea aged 18 to 30 (35 for Canadians): 12 months, at most six with one employer, and it cannot be converted in Spain.
atlas-es.0214: Up to 90 days in any 180, with no paid work. At the border you may be asked to show about €122 a day, at least €1,098.90. Arriving through another Schengen airport, declare your entry at a police station within 72 working hours and keep your boarding passes.
atlas-es.0215: Beckham regime for people moving to Spain
atlas-es.0216: A flat 24% tax on up to €600,000 of employment income for the year of arrival and five more, if you were not tax-resident in Spain for the previous five years and moved for the job. Coming first to study and then being hired does not qualify.
atlas-es.0217: Book police appointments (cita previa) only through the official site or an accredited lawyer: appointments sold by bots or middlemen are refused at the door when the names do not match, and can bring criminal charges.
atlas-es.0218: With an approved work authorisation, you have 1 month to apply for the D visa at the Spanish consulate (€80), with an apostilled criminal record under 90 days old and a medical certificate.
atlas-es.0219: Register on the town hall’s population register (empadronamiento) with your passport and lease: everyone resident must, and the town hall may not demand a NIE first. The certificate is accepted for 3 months in immigration paperwork.
atlas-es.0220: Within 3 months, get the EU registration certificate (CUE) at the police (form EX-18, €12), with your ID, the register certificate and your employer’s Social Security enrolment; it carries your definitive NIE.
atlas-es.0221: It is a green paper card with no photo: always show it with your passport or ID, and never laminate it, which voids it.
atlas-es.0222: Within 30 days of your Social Security enrolment, book a fingerprint appointment for the foreigner’s identity card (TIE): form EX-17 and fee 790-012, €16.08.
atlas-es.0223: Ask for your Social Security number (NUSS) online at Import@ss with your passport, before the job starts. A white NIE certificate (€9.84) is only a tax number, not a residence right.
atlas-es.0224: Employees, researchers and interns are enrolled free in the national health service and get the individual health card (TSI).
atlas-es.0225: Legal residents not working and without private cover can join the public scheme (convenio especial) after 12 months on the population register: €60 a month under 65.
atlas-es.0226: Keep your population-register entry current: registering at an address where you do not live leads to removal from the register and criminal charges for false documents.
atlas-es.0227: Renew your population-register entry every 2 years, or it is cancelled and breaks the continuity you need for renewals and citizenship.
atlas-es.0228: The renewal receipt keeps your stay and right to work, but is not valid for travel in Schengen: for a trip, ask the police for a return authorisation (about €10.72), and fly direct to and from a non-Schengen country.
atlas-es.0229: With an expired card and only the renewal receipt you may not travel in the Schengen area. A return authorisation lets you fly only directly between Spain and your home country, with no Schengen stopover.
atlas-es.0230: Police appointments sold online by bots or middlemen (€50 to €250) can be refused at the door when the names do not match, and buying them can be a crime.
atlas-es.0231: Non-EU residents without long-term residence must renew their town-hall registration every two years, or it is cancelled and the years stop counting.
atlas-es.0232: A town-hall registration at an address where you do not live, or a fake job contract, is a crime that can cost the permit and lead to removal.
atlas-es.0233: Never laminate the green EU certificate: it becomes void. Always carry it with your passport or identity card.
atlas-es.0234: Some universities mention 24 months for the job-search permit; the law says 12, not extendable.
atlas-es.0235: PhD students funded entirely by a foreign government are handled differently depending on whether the university signs a hosting agreement.
atlas-es.0236: Approval by silence is the law, but banks and payroll often wait for the formal certificate, which takes another 30 to 60 days.
atlas-es.0237: Middlemen still capture police appointment slots despite one-time SMS codes and bot filters.
atlas-es.0238: Whether the Beckham regime applies after an online Spanish master taken from abroad is not settled by the tax authority.
